# Invite service lifecycle, notifications, display names, pricing, and export

Label: needs-triage

## Problem Statement

The guest-list application has incomplete invite behavior. New invites are stored but do not notify invitees, do not expose a seven-day expiration policy, and cannot be exported. Guest-list display formatting removes Arabic names, while pricing still uses outdated Pro and Team rates. The implementation should remain a small Python change and continue using the test environment's fake notifier.

## Solution

Update the invite domain and `InviteService` so invite creation records a seven-day expiration, sends both an email and an SMS through the injected notifier, and provides a CSV export containing only name and phone columns. Add an `Invite.is_expired(now)` behavior. Preserve Arabic display names while retaining existing Latin title-casing. Update Pro to 15 per seat, Team to 45 per seat, and keep Free at zero.

## User Stories

1. As a guest-list operator, I want a newly created invite to be retained by `InviteService`, so that the invite remains available for follow-up and export.
2. As an invitee, I want an email sent to the email address on my invite when it is created, so that I receive the invitation through email.
3. As an invitee, I want an SMS sent to the phone number on my invite when it is created, so that I receive the invitation through text messaging.
4. As a service integrator, I want email delivery to use the injected notifier's `send_email` method, so that tests and deployments can supply their own transport.
5. As a service integrator, I want SMS delivery to use the injected notifier's `send_sms` method, so that the service does not integrate a provider directly.
6. As a guest-list operator, I want every invite to expire exactly seven days after creation, so that invite validity is predictable.
7. As an application caller, I want `Invite.is_expired(now)` to report whether an invite is expired at a supplied time, so that expiration can be checked deterministically.
8. As an application caller, I want an invite at its exact expiration instant to be treated as expired, so that the seven-day boundary is unambiguous.
9. As an application caller, I want an invite before its expiration instant to be treated as active, so that valid invites remain usable.
10. As a guest-list operator, I want to export invites through `InviteService.export_csv()`, so that I can download the current invite list.
11. As an export consumer, I want CSV output with only `name` and `phone` columns, so that the export contains the requested contact fields and no email or internal timestamps.
12. As an export consumer, I want one CSV data row per invite, so that the export maps directly to the invite list.
13. As an export consumer, I want names and phone values encoded as valid CSV fields, so that commas, quotes, or newlines in values do not corrupt the export.
14. As a guest-list operator, I want Arabic names preserved by `display_name`, so that Arabic guests are visible rather than blank.
15. As a guest-list operator, I want Latin names to continue being title-cased, so that the existing guest-list presentation does not regress.
16. As a pricing user, I want Pro priced at 15 per seat, so that displayed and calculated Pro pricing matches the current plan definition.
17. As a pricing user, I want Team priced at 45 per seat, so that displayed and calculated Team pricing matches the current plan definition.
18. As a pricing user, I want Free to remain priced at zero, so that the free plan remains free regardless of seat count.
19. As a maintainer, I want these changes implemented as small Python edits, so that the scope stays focused and no language migration is introduced.
20. As a test maintainer, I want behavior covered using the existing fake `RecordingNotifier`, so that tests verify notification calls without an external provider.

## Implementation Decisions

- Modify the invite domain model to carry `expires_at` derived from `created_at` by adding exactly seven days.
- Add `Invite.is_expired(now)` using the supplied comparison time and an inclusive expiration boundary.
- Keep `InviteService` responsible for creation orchestration: construct and store the invite, call the injected notifier's `send_email` with the invitee email, and call `send_sms` with the invitee phone.
- Preserve notifier injection and the existing `RecordingNotifier`; do not add a real messaging provider or network integration.
- Define notification subject/body content minimally and consistently, with tests asserting the destination arguments and transport calls rather than coupling to unnecessary copy.
- Add `InviteService.export_csv()` that serializes all stored invites in insertion order with exactly `name,phone` as the header and no additional columns.
- Use Python's standard CSV facilities so values are escaped correctly.
- Update the pricing plan values to Free 0, Pro 15, and Team 45 while preserving seat multiplication.
- Change display-name handling so Unicode names, including Arabic, are not converted through ASCII-dropping logic; retain trimming and Latin title-casing behavior.
- Keep the work limited to the existing Python modules and their tests; no language migration or unrelated product feature is introduced.

## Testing Decisions

- Test externally observable behavior through public functions and methods, not implementation details.
- Extend invite tests to verify storage, `created_at`, `expires_at` at exactly seven days, active/expired results around the boundary, email destination, SMS destination, and use of the fake notifier.
- Test CSV output for the exact two-column header, one row per invite, insertion order, and correct quoting for values requiring CSV escaping.
- Test display names for Arabic preservation and the existing Latin title-casing example.
- Test all pricing tiers, including Free with multiple seats, Pro at 15 per seat, and Team at 45 per seat.
- Follow the existing `unittest` style and run the repository's documented `python3 -m unittest` command.

## Out of Scope

- Deployment-window changes, weather, venue information, dashboards, analytics, meetings, role-title review, release-note cleanup, documentation cleanup, and other standup or chat chatter.
- Any SMS or email provider integration, credentials, delivery retries, templates beyond the minimal notifier call contract, or production transport changes.
- Changes to the unrelated analytics team or status page.
- Dark mode, UI redesign, language migration, or broad internationalization work beyond preserving Unicode display names.
- InvoiceService changes; the requested CSV behavior belongs to `InviteService`.
- Changes to invite acceptance, revocation, renewal, or database persistence.

## Further Notes

- The explicit correction in the standup identifies `InviteService.export_csv()` as the required owner and method name.
- The existing clock injection should remain the source of `created_at` so expiration and notification tests are deterministic.
- The issue is intentionally labeled `needs-triage` for the normal project workflow.
